questions.q: What does Munger mean by staying inside your circle of competence?
a: Sticking to what you understand and accepting your limits
Following the advice of stock analysts
questions.why: Lesson 1 says good investors admit what they do not know and avoid businesses they cannot grasp.

questions.q: What three buckets does Berkshire Hathaway use for potential investments?
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the third bucket as ideas that might work later but are not understood well enough yet.

questions.q: What does “Don't just do something, stand there” advise investors to do?
a: Wait patiently for the right company
Trade often to capture quick gains
questions.why: Lesson 2 says suitable companies are rare, so most of an investor's time should be spent waiting.

questions.q: Why do restless investors end up worse off, according to the summary?
a: They pile up losses, fees, and taxes
They miss the market's best years
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts constant trading with the great investor who makes a few right trades and waits.

questions.q: What is worldly wisdom built from?
a: Mental models drawn from many disciplines
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes lenses from psychology, history, biology and other fields that can be combined as needed.
